text.p: Indonesian PT Intraco Penta said on Monday a company with related business lines had expressed interest in acquiring a stake in the heavy equipment distributor.
"We are still considering the possibility. We are planning to have the first meeting with the interested party within a few weeks," Penta's finance director Petrus Halim told Reuters.
"They have already expressed an interest in acquiring a stake in our firm, but so far nothing has been fixed," he said
Shares of Penta rose 15 percent, or 225 rupiah, to 1,725 rupiah, in active afternoon trading on Monday following a rise of around 50 percent last week.
Petrus declined to give further details but said the interested party had related business lines.

"The interested party has related business lines with Penta. For example, we are engaged in heavy equipment distributorship and the interested party may be a toll road operator which could use the equipment," he said.
Penta sent a letter to the stock exchange authorities last week denying market talk that it had reached an acquisition deal, Petrus said.
Petrus said Penta was considering the possibility of splitting the company stock's nominal value to 500 rupiah from the current 1,000 rupiah.
"The stock split plan is considered necessary so as to further boost the liquidity of our shares on the stock market," he said.
He said the firm was also considering announcing a rights issue for 1997 to increase working capital and finance expansion, but he declined to give details.
Penta posted a net profit of 1.1 billion rupiah in the first-half of 1996 against 1.7 billion rupiah in the same period of last year.
